name: Wimberley Market Days
desc: First-Saturday open-air market running March through December. Booth spaces are assigned by seniority, with a rolling waitlist for new vendors. Approval is rolling via email (leasing@wimberleymarketday.com), not a fixed application deadline; booths are typically rented the week before each market day.

name: Fredericksburg Trade Days
desc: Three-day Hill Country market held the third weekend of each month across covered barns and open field lots. Pricing varies by space: $75-$135 for outdoor lots, $150-$273 for indoor barn spaces (10x14 to 15x14). No published application deadline or jury process; contact 210-846-4094 to book.

name: Bayou City Art Festival
desc: Juried fine art festival drawing a national applicant pool across 19 media categories. Panel review with blind scoring. This is the Memorial Park edition (Fri-Sun); booth fees range $525-$1775 by category/size plus a separate $50 non-refundable jury fee. Accepted artists notified by Jul 6. Public admission is $18 early-bird/$20 regular per day (kids 6-12 $5, 5 and under free), or $30 for a weekend pass.

name: Comicpalooza
desc: Multi-genre pop culture convention with a dedicated Artist Alley. Tables sell out in tiers; early registration opens to prior-year vendors. UNVERIFIED: 2027 exhibitor applications aren't open yet (interest form only as of Aug 2026) — no official 2027 dates, pricing, or deadline published. Current start/end/deadline/fee below are unconfirmed placeholders.

name: Armadillo Christmas Bazaar
desc: Ten-day juried holiday art market with live music. Long-run format favors vendors with deep inventory and staffing help. Booth fees run ~$1,500-$5,000+ by size (avg ~$2,000) plus a $25 application fee. Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis; Jan-Mar submissions get priority, with primary review Mar-Aug. Returning artists get priority over new applicants in popular categories. Public admission is $12 (+fees, ~$14 total) per day, or $60 for a season pass; kids 12 and under free.

name: First Monday Trade Days
desc: One of the largest recurring open-air markets in the country, spanning several hundred acres over four days each month. UNVERIFIED: the grounds are split across many independently-operated pavilions, each with its own booth pricing and contact — there is no single official fee. Call the City of Canton First Monday office at 903-567-6556 for a specific venue's rate.

name: Cottonwood Art Festival
desc: Twice-yearly juried fine art festival in a shaded park setting. Jury reviews three work images plus one booth shot. $500 covers a single booth; a double booth is $1,000 (limited) and electricity is a $100 add-on. A separate $35 non-refundable jury/application fee is paid per entry via ZAPPlication.

name: Blue Genie Art Bazaar
desc: Consignment-model holiday bazaar. No booth fee or staffing requirement; the venue takes a percentage of sales instead. The Yelp "Temporarily Closed" status is normal seasonal downtime, not a shutdown — the storefront is a holiday-only operation that reopens each November for the season (confirmed reopening November 2026), consistent with this listing's window. Public admission is believed free (multiple secondary sources agree; the official FAQ page returned a 404 during verification, so treat as likely rather than confirmed).

name: Anime Matsuri
desc: Anime and Japanese culture convention with a large artist alley and separate dealer hall. Table assignment by registration order. Corrected from a stale March placeholder — Anime Matsuri actually runs in July; the 2026 edition (Jul 23-26) is confirmed and uncancelled, and 2027 is set for Jul 22-25 (per Eventbrite, though organizers note dates may shift). Applications open Sept 8 with price tiers increasing Dec 1/Mar 1/Jun 1 - exact table price not published outside the application form, so the $380 figure and Dec 1 "deadline" (first price-increase date) are best-effort estimates.

name: Main Street Fort Worth Arts Festival
desc: Four-day juried street festival with very high foot traffic. Booths are on pavement; weights required in place of stakes. Standard 10x10 booth is $995 (corner $1,145), plus a separate $40 non-refundable application fee. Roughly 200 artists are jury-selected from nearly 1,000 applicants.

name: Emerald City Comic Con
desc: Artist Alley is curated via portfolio review, not a lottery or first-come order. Accepted artists get a 6' table plus 2 badges for $430, due in full by the January deadline to hold the space. 2027 applications are already closed as of this writing; a waitlist is available.

name: Round Top Antiques Fair
desc: Roughly two-and-a-half-week destination market spread across 48+ independent show fields (not nine days as previously listed). Early fields like Bar W Field, Henkel Square, and The Marketplace Warrenton open Oct 15; most of the 48+ venues run the official Oct 17-31 window. Space is leased directly from individual field operators (e.g. Zapp Hall, Excess Fields, Marburger Farm, Big Red Barn) - pricing and application process vary by field and remain unconfirmed here; the $900 fee is an unverified placeholder. Public admission is similarly fragmented across the 48+ fields — most are free to browse, but the flagship "Original Round Top Antiques Fair" field charges its own $10 general/$25 VIP admission, so no single admission price applies to the market as a whole.

name: Texas Renaissance Festival
desc: Eight-weekend seasonal festival requiring period-appropriate merchandise and shop presentation. Multi-season vendors get renewal priority. Confirmed: the vendor application itself carries a $50 non-refundable fee. The $1,400 figure here is presumed to be the actual shop/booth lease, but I could not confirm that number from the source PDF (binary-encoded, didn't extract cleanly) — needs a second look. Public admission is NOT free — gate pricing varies by weekend, roughly $20-25 (advance, early weekends) to ~$29 (later weekends, at the gate), but the official ticket page didn't load cleanly during verification, so treat this range as a rough ballpark, not confirmed.

name: Austin Flea
desc: Recurring indie maker pop-up hosted at rotating bars and venues. Low entry cost makes it a common first market for new vendors. Booths run $50-$75/event (varies by venue, listed per application) plus a $5/yr new-vendor tent/display approval fee. Each application is individually juried; Texas Sales Tax Permit required. Local, handmade/vintage sellers only — no imported goods.

name: Dallas Fan Expo
desc: Large pop culture convention with tiered artist alley pricing by table location and corner access. Corrected from a placeholder May 2027 date - the confirmed, upcoming edition is Sep 11-13, 2026 at the Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center (2027 dates aren't announced yet). Standard 6x5 table is $480; premium 5x12 end-cap is $1,060. No fixed application deadline is published - tables sell until they run out, so this date is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. Public single-day admission was showing Fri $33/Sat $58/Sun $48 on the official site at verification time, but these are time-limited advance-pricing promos, not a stable figure — left unconfirmed here rather than embedding a price that'll go stale.

name: Nutcracker Market
desc: Massive juried holiday shopping market fundraising for Houston Ballet, drawing over 100,000 shoppers across a preview party plus four show days at NRG Center. Unlike a flat booth-fee model, Houston Ballet also takes an 11% commission on merchant sales on top of space cost, and charges a separate non-refundable $25 application fee. Exact booth pricing tiers weren't accessible (pricing page blocked automated access), so the $2,500 fee here is a rough placeholder based on comparable high-traffic juried holiday markets, not a confirmed price - confirm real pricing and the application deadline directly before applying. Public admission is $20/day general, or $60 for a 4-day early-bird pass; kids 2 and under free.

name: Denton Arts & Jazz Festival
desc: Long-running juried art show paired with a large free jazz festival, recently relocated to the North Texas Fairgrounds and shifted from its traditional spring slot to Sep 11-13, 2026 (worth double-checking before relying on the old April date elsewhere). 10x10 booths available indoor/outdoor; a $50/exhibitor surcharge applies for shared booths. Jun 1 is the no-surcharge cutoff, not a hard close - late fees of $20 (after Jun 1) and $50 (after Aug 1) suggest applications are still accepted this close to the show, just at a premium; the Aug 20 date here is an estimated last-call, not an official cutoff. Base booth fee was never published anywhere I could find - the $300 here is an unverified estimate, not a confirmed price. Attendance (~200k) is the festival's historical figure from its old Quakertown Park venue and may not hold at the new fairgrounds site.

name: Boerne Market Days
desc: Recurring Hill Country market on Boerne's historic Main Plaza, held the second weekend of every month (plus a bonus December date not reflected in this listing's auto-computed schedule). Vendors reapply each month they want to participate. Booth fees must be paid by the 1st of the month before the show and are non-refundable, but the actual dollar amount isn't published online - the $40 here is a rough estimate based on comparable small-town Hill Country markets, not a confirmed price. Contact davidquerbach@eventsoffmain.com or (210) 844-8193 to confirm current pricing and attendance before applying. Public admission is inferred free — the official page lists public market hours with no fee mentioned, but there's no explicit "free" statement either.
